newsitem.title: USA: Rock-Tenn sees $1.5-$2 mln charges in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Rock-Tenn sees $1.5-$2 mln charges in Q3.

text.p: Rock-Tenn Co said Friday it expects to take a third-quarter after-tax charge of $1.5 to $2 million for the shut-down of the company's folding carton plant in Mundelein, Ill.
Rock-Tenn also said it will delay until market conditions improve a previously announced public offering of equity securities planned for the first half of 1997.
Rock-Tenn on Friday reported a second-quarter loss of $0.22 per share, or $7.2 million, versus a $0.36 per share, or $12.3 million profit in the same quarter a year earlier.

The company said it took an after-tax charge of $12.8 million, or $0.38 per share, in the second quarter associated with the closing of the plant, which is closing in order to consolidate operations following the acquisition of Waldorf Corp. in January 1997.
The company said its second quarter was hurt by industry overcapacity, slow growth and competition.
The company said the proceeds from the proposed public offering were to be used to repay a portion of the borrowings incurred by the company in connection with the Waldorf acquisition.
